patient_information: A 35-year-old Malawian woman, divorced, with three children, works as a small-scale farmer and sells vegetables, able to afford three meals a day with occasional meat or fish.
history_of_present_illness: Fever started 3 days earlier; weakness progressed over several months. She reported weight loss but no cough, night sweats, diarrhoea, dysuria, or abnormal bleeds. Two months prior, she was prescribed iron tablets for weakness and pallor, which she took without improvement.
exposure_and_epidemiology: A 35-year-old woman from Malawi, a high-prevalence setting for HIV in sub-Saharan Africa.
vitals: Blood pressure 90/60 mmHg, pulse 110 bpm, temperature 37.8°C (100°F), respiratory rate 25 breaths/min, oxygen saturation 97% on ambient air, Glasgow Coma Scale 15/15.
physical_exam: Wasted (BMI 17kg/m²), very pale conjunctivae, no jaundice. Normal mouth, clear chest. Abdomen soft with slight diffuse tenderness and no guarding. Spleen palpable 3 cm below the left costal margin. Normal rectal examination.
labs_and_diagnostics: Malaria rapid diagnostic test negative, HIV serology positive, and full blood count showed WBC 3.0 ×10^9/L, Haemoglobin 4.8 mg/dL, MCV 90 fL, Platelets 112 ×10^9/L. Blood cultures grew Salmonella enterica var Typhimurium. TB screening revealed prominent hilar lymph nodes.
differential_diagnosis: Sepsis without a clear focus, advanced immunosuppression with possible concomitant tuberculosis (TB), invasive non-typhoidal Salmonellae (iNTS), enteric fevers (typhoid or paratyphoid), iron deficiency, helminth infections, malaria, and visceral leishmaniasis.
management_and_clinical_course: Initially treated with IV ceftriaxone 2g od and fluid resuscitation. After Salmonella enterica var Typhimurium was identified, antibiotic treatment was changed to oral ciprofloxacin 500mg tds for 14 days. She was also commenced on antituberculous treatment, antiretroviral therapy, co-trimoxazole prophylaxis, vitamin B6, and therapeutic feeding. She was discharged after 4 weeks and at 3-month follow-up, was feeling better, gained weight, and had improving haemoglobin levels.
final_diagnosis: Invasive non-typhoidal Salmonellae (iNTS) infection, HIV infection, and tuberculosis.
disease_name_short: Invasive Non-Typhoidal Salmonellae Infection, HIV, and Tuberculosis.
